adopted.CLAUDE.md: adopted in full. This repo keeps no decision docs — docs/ holds plans and transient review artifacts only — and the source's § "Writing things down" routes a decision's alternatives to the PR or issue thread, which is what this repo already does. /audit-github-backlog carries the last upstream mention of decision docs, and it is declined.

adopted..claude/skills/sync-upstream/: this skill, renamed .claude/skills/sync-agent-boilerplate/ after the one source this repo has.

adopted.scripts/vet.sh: rewritten for this stack: pnpm build alone and first (it regenerates .next/types/, which tsconfig includes), then styles:codegen alone, then the rest fanned out through run-parallel.sh. CLAUDE.md § Vetting carries the roster and why each check sits where it does. Read the source's edits for the idea; the file itself never lands.

declined..claude/skills/implement/: the source's redirect stub pointing /implement at /go, declined on the operator's call at the sync that renamed the skill: a permanent extra row is not worth keeping a retired name resolvable. `/plan` writes `/go <branch>` handoff blocks, and an older block saying `/implement` is a word an agent reads, not a skill it must load. Never — the stub only ever earns its place in the window right after the rename, and that window is closed
declined.ADOPTING.md: the source's guide for a repo taking the boilerplate on, which this repo did once and will not do again. Revisit only if a repo ever adopts from here — it would need its own, not a copy of the source's
declined.docs/catalog.md: never — the source's own inventory of what it ships, describing the upstream boilerplate rather than this repo. Step 4a reads it from the clone, where it is current by construction; a vendored copy would only drift. CLAUDE.md § "Adding or renaming a skill" records that check-skill-catalog.sh skips its catalog assertions here for the same reason
declined..claude/skills/propose-issue/: issues are opened by hand here, and the backlog is too small to dedupe against — revisit when filing becomes routine
declined..claude/skills/audit-github-backlog/: the backlog is a handful of issues an operator can read in one sitting — revisit when it is large enough that a sweep beats reading it
declined..claude/skills/release/: merging to main deploys automatically; there is no versioned release to cut
declined..claude/skills/hotfix/: no promotion path to bypass — main deploys straight to Pages
declined..claude/skills/log-review/: static site on GitHub Pages; there are no deployed logs to read
declined..claude/skills/test-on-gh/: nothing runs on pull requests here, and the whole suite is fast enough to sit in the vet fan-out, so there is no bucket too slow or too heavy for a local run to dispatch to CI. A test suite existing is not the condition — this is. Revisit if one appears that needs a browser, a service, or minutes rather than seconds
declined..claude/skills/bootstrap-workflow-dispat: the one dispatchable workflow here, deploy.yml, has been on main since before its workflow_dispatch trigger existed, so Actions metadata already knows it and the 404 this skill clears cannot occur. It also @-references the declined /test-on-gh, so adopting it would break the closure check. Revisit when a new dispatch-only workflow is added — likely alongside /test-on-gh
